rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The **scalar triple product** [a b c] = a·(b × c) — the component determinant — measures **signed volume**: |[a b c]| is the parallelepiped's volume (NEB 2024's definition-and-significance answer), ⅙ of it the tetrahedron's, and **zero exactly for coplanar** vectors. It is **cyclically invariant** ([a b c] = [b c a] = [c a b]) and **sign-flipping** under any single swap.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
[a b c] = a·(b × c) = |a₁ a₂ a₃; b₁ b₂ b₃; c₁ c₂ c₃| = (a × b)·c
|[a b c]| = parallelepiped volume; tetrahedron Ⅵ... ⅙|[a b c]|

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "[a b c] = a.(b x c); |[a b c]| is the parallelepiped volume; a x (b x c) = (a.c)b - (a.b)c."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***BAC-CAB in the plane*** — a x (b x c) always lands in the plane of b and c: the identity's right side contains only b and c, no a.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The scalar triple product is base-times-height in one symbol: cross for the base area, dot for the height - volume with a sign.  ·  a × (b × c) = (a·c)b − (a·b)c

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Volume in One Number The **scalar triple product** [a b c] = a·(b × c) turns three vectors into a signed volume; the **vector triple product** a × (b × c) stays a vector and obeys the **BAC–CAB rule**. Their theorems: the determinant form, the coplanarity criterion, the volume theorem, and the two expansion rules.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Scalar triple product - **Definition:** [a b c] = a·(b × c) — a scalar. - **Determinant form:** [a b c] = |a₁ a₂ a₃; b₁ b₂ b₃; c₁ c₂ c₃|. - **Theorem (volume):** |[a b c]| = volume of the **parallelepiped** with coterminous edges a, b, c; **one-sixth** of it is the tetrahedron's volume. - **Theorem (coplanarity):** a, b, c are coplanar ⟺ **[a b c] = 0**.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Coplanarity: determinant = 0. Volume: |determinant|; tetrahedron: divide by 6. Swaps flip sign; rotations keep it. BAC-CAB: (a.c)b - (a.b)c - c pairs with b.

rows.text: **NEB 2024 (verified PYQ): What is the scalar triple product? Write its geometric significance. (2m)** — **Definition:** for three vectors a, b, c the **scalar triple product** is **[a b c] = a·(b × c)** — the scalar obtained by dotting one vector with the cross product of the other two.…  ·  **NEB-style (3m): Prove the cyclic invariance [a b c] = [b c a] = [c a b] and that interchanging two vectors reverses the sign.** — **Determinant route:** [a b c] is the determinant of the matrix with rows a, b, c. **Cyclic rotation** of the rows (a,b,c → b,c,a) is achieved by **two** row interchanges: (a,b,c) → (b,a,c) → (b,c,a).…

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Scalar triple product: [a b c] = a.(b x c) = determinant of components = (a x b).c. Volume theorem: |[a b c]| = parallelepiped volume; tetrahedron = (1/6)|[a b c]|. Coplanarity: [a b c] = 0. Cyclic invariance: [a b c] = [b c a] = [c a b]; any swap flips sign. Dot and cross interchangeable: a.(b x c) = (a x b).c.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Determinant sign conventions in linear algebra (row swaps flip sign) are the triple product's cyclic law generalised.

rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): Verify the BAC–CAB rule for a = î, b = ĵ, c = k̂.** — **Left side:** b × c = ĵ × k̂ = î, so a × (b × c) = î × î = **0**. **Right side:** (a·c)b − (a·b)c = (î·k̂)ĵ − (î·ĵ)k̂ = (0)ĵ − (0)k̂ = **0**. Both sides agree ✓.…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 6. Common Confusions **Cyclic, not any permutation:** [b a c] = −[a b c] — only rotations keep the sign.  ·  **BAC–CAB order:** a × (b × c) = (a·c)b − (a·b)c — the dot product with **c** multiplies **b**; reversing pairs is the classic slip.  ·  **Tetrahedron factor:** ⅙ of the parallelepiped volume, not ½ (that is the triangle's share of the parallelogram).

rows.text: ## 7. Exam Application **NEB 2024 (verified PYQ): What is the scalar triple product? Write its geometric significance. (2m)** — For vectors a, b, c the **scalar triple product** is **[a b c] = a·(b × c)** — the dot product of one vector with the cross product of the other two; in components it is the determinant |a₁…  ·  **NEB-style (3m): Show that the vectors a = î + ĵ + k̂, b = 2î + 3ĵ − k̂... coplanarity via [a b c] = 0 (template).** — Assemble the component determinant and expand; zero ⟹ coplanar (one vector is a combination of the other two), non-zero ⟹ they span space with volume |[a b c]|.  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Verify BAC–CAB for a = î, b = ĵ, c = ĵ.** — Left: a × (b × c) = î × (ĵ × ĵ) = î × 0 = **0**. Right: (a·c)b − (a·b)c = (î·ĵ)ĵ − (î·ĵ)ĵ = 0 − 0 = **0** ✓. Both sides agree; the identity holds even in degenerate cases.
